coverage: A signed managed descriptor is now accepted by the market staging path and appears in the release catalogue as backend, installable metadata.
The management install plan and commit select the managed review/consumer from canonical plan bytes instead of falling through to the static path.
Without a configured or compatible runner, managed install admission fails with a bounded runtime-unavailable response and creates no installation or operation.
The development static .portalapp envelope has an exact three-member format, bounded ZIP parser, closed detached-signature syntax, exact descriptor/frontend binding and inspector output.
The Apps packer emits deterministic envelopes from already signed bytes and never reads a private key.
The administrator offline upload stages through existing trust/signature/immutable-release checks, then completes the normal review, commit, activation and launch path on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
Unknown, duplicate, traversal, symlink, executable, changed-frontend, wrong-digest, malformed and frontend-only managed envelopes are refused without state.
limits: The static offline envelope is implemented, but managed OCI image layout/platform payloads and public envelope-format freeze remain open.

coverage: A validly signed managed descriptor whose OCI image digest is changed afterward is refused before the staged-release callback runs.
A changed descriptor, signature, version, frontend artifact, publisher policy or namespace is refused with no durable mutation.
limits: This is the repository admission boundary, not a replacement against a live production installation.

coverage: The shared Go and TypeScript publisher corpus contains 55 cases with exact frame SHA-256 f0553de5a701b0d8f665a2e997a525c8022ba5039ab6bce4c62da18f3118d641.
Wrong key, namespace, algorithm, key revision, disabled publisher, expired key and revoked key are refused.
Catalogue discovery returns publisher_verified false; catalogue metadata alone does not establish trust.

Traversal, absolute and backslash paths, encoded separators, dot normalization, duplicate and case-colliding entries, file/directory conflicts, symlinks, devices, setuid entries, executables, server programs and unknown media are refused.
Archive, per-file, total-byte and entry-count limits are independent; CRC failures, forged ZIP metadata, ZIP64, multi-disk and trailing data are refused.
Inspection is in memory and returns no partial file metadata on failure; the package tools reject symlinked roots and private or non-regular assets.
Platform API ranges, runner protocol, runtime architecture and backend protocol mismatches are refused.
A managed package without a compatible runner is refused before installation admission.
Invalid descriptor/schema versions, missing architectures and unsupported requirements return bounded refusal results.
limits: The compatibility target is the development host contract, not a full matrix of deployed runner versions.

coverage: Changing publisher trust, policy revision or the stored target package while an update review is open makes the old confirmation unusable.
The live source release remains active and no update operation is admitted after refusal.
Install reviews reject trust changes, role demotion, altered plan JSON, wrong plan digests and an older unfinished installation.
limits: Catalogue URL metadata is discovery-only. A catalogue edit cannot replace the exact signed bytes already bound by digest.

coverage: Replaying identical immutable bytes is idempotent and creates one release plus one frontend artifact.
Changing executable descriptor bytes for an already published app/version is refused.
Failed or refused staging leaves the old release assets and trust records unchanged.

commands: Disposable app-project-quota-probe run 41599541528/job 125794746175 executes interrupted managed staging and restart recovery
coverage: A truncated artifact response retains its bounded in-memory prefix for the same fetch. The retry sends Range and If-Range; a valid 206 continues at the exact offset, while a 200 safely restarts from zero. Redirects retain the range headers and final descriptor, signature and frontend digest checks still decide admission.
Exhausting the bounded retry budget leaves no staged release.
Replaying an already staged immutable package reuses the existing release without creating another operation.
Mutating an already staged frontend artifact is detected by the stored-release recheck before admission.

A real managed writable installation was interrupted after its side-effect-free stage boundary. A new scheduler reclaimed the same operation under a higher fence and completed real data, candidate start, readiness/registration and activation with one applied copy of every durable effect.
A file-backed SQLite database with the freelist exhausted and no page-growth allowance refuses a roughly 1 MiB package; release, frontend and staging-audit rows all roll back.
limits: The received prefix exists only in memory for one bounded fetch. There is no persistent market cache, so request termination or process restart starts the next fetch at offset zero.
Persistent cache design and approval remain open; no cache table or unmanaged cache file has been added.

commands: Disposable app-project-quota-probe run 41594944957/job 125779995923 executes the native package-revocation stop and recovery path
coverage: Publisher disable or key revocation verifies active signed releases and atomically queues the existing reviewed disable path for affected ready installations.
Static quarantine immediately denies launch and the existing scheduler reaches complete without dropping the dedicated plugin table.

Managed quarantine preserves runtime identity, namespace and data, advances the writer fence and queues managed stop; an unavailable runner records managed_disable_unavailable rather than claiming a stop.

A native publisher policy revocation initiated the queue and the real disposable runner reached a successful stop. Restoring trust and explicitly enabling or repairing reverified the same signed release under the current trust revision instead of accepting stale revision evidence.
Repeated revocation does not duplicate quarantine operations, and launch refusal does not read executable content.
limits: The native stop is development evidence on the disposable GitHub Linux root runner, not production deployment approval.
Trust is deployment-local. There is no external trust fetch to make unreachable; a failed local trust read must continue to fail closed.

coverage: The descriptor corpus contains 56 exact shared cases and the publisher corpus contains 55 exact shared cases.
Go and TypeScript consume the same bytes and expect the same acceptance or refusal for each shared descriptor and signature vector.
The Python package builder now invokes the same TypeScript validator in a corpus mode pinned to the exact 56-case descriptor hash.
All 56 Python packaging and publication tests pass, including deterministic archives, path safety and signed-release provenance.
limits: The public package format and protocol error vocabulary remain development contracts pending formal freeze.
